title: Fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes
subtitle: tall, tender diner-style pancakes with butter and real maple syrup
imageAlt: A tall stack of golden buttermilk pancakes with butter and maple syrup on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: about 12 pancakes: breakfast for two, plus 2 more for tomorrow

beforeYouStart.text: Don't overmix: a few lumps make tall, tender pancakes.
Medium heat, not high. The first pancake is a test; adjust the heat after it.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.

steps.title: Wet
steps.text: Whisk the buttermilk, eggs, melted butter and vanilla in another bowl.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet into the dry and stir just until no dry flour shows; lumps are good. Rest 5 minutes while the pan heats.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat a large nonstick skillet or griddle over medium and wipe with a little oil. Pour ¼ cup batter per pancake. Cook 2–3 minutes until bubbles pop on top and the edges look set, flip and cook 1–2 minutes more until golden and springy in the centre. Repeat, oiling the pan as needed.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Stack them hot with butter and warm maple syrup.

fixIt.fix: The batter was overmixed or the baking powder is old; stir less and check the date.
The pan is too hot; turn it down a notch and cook a little longer.
Stir 2 tbsp lemon juice or white vinegar into 2 cups milk and let it stand 5 minutes.

saleTip: Buttermilk is about $2.49 a litre at No Frills; freeze the rest in 1-cup portions for the next batch.
swap: Whole wheat flour for half the flour. Milk soured with lemon juice for buttermilk.
leftovers: Freeze extra pancakes flat between parchment; toast them straight from frozen on a weekday.
doneness: Cook until springy in the centre with no wet batter; the eggs in the batter cook through as they set (Health Canada, egg dishes to 74°C / 165°F).
source: Based on tested buttermilk pancake methods (Canadian Living, America's Test Kitchen): a thick lumpy batter with baking powder and soda, rested 5 minutes and cooked on a medium griddle.
prepAhead: Mix the dry ingredients the night before and cover.
Cooked pancakes freeze up to 2 months.
reheat: From the fridge or freezer: toaster or microwave 30–60 seconds until hot, 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Plain pancakes with butter and syrup; no vanilla.

fancy.note: Blueberry pancakes with maple whipped cream.

stepNotes.3: Fancy: scatter a few blueberries onto each pancake right after pouring.

addSteps.title: Maple cream
addSteps.text: Whip the cream with 1 tbsp maple syrup to soft peaks and spoon over the stacks.

plating: Stack three high, berries on top.
A spoon of maple cream and a drizzle of syrup.
Warm the syrup in a small jug.

why.0-5: Buttermilk's acid reacts with the baking soda for extra lift and a tender crumb.
why.0-2: Baking powder adds a second rise on the griddle so they stay tall.

funFact: Canada makes about 70% of the world's maple syrup, most of it in Quebec.

keeps.thaw: No need to thaw: toast or microwave straight from frozen until hot

drink: Hot coffee or tea and a glass of cold milk; orange juice on a weekend.
